chunks: And whatever is in it from al-Ṣabāḥ ibn Siyābah, I have narrated it from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan—may Allah be pleased with him—from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr al-Bajalī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ṣabāḥ ibn Siyābah, the brother of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Siyābah al-Kūfī.

key_terms.الصَّبَاحِ بْنِ سِيَابَةَ: A transmitter whose narrations are being linked through this chain.
key_terms.الصَّفَّارِ: A key transmitter in the chain, referring to Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār.
key_terms.الْبَجَلِيِّ: A tribal attribution identifying Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr al-Bajalī.
key_terms.الْكُوفِيِّ: A geographical attribution indicating association with Kūfah.
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I have transmitted it; a statement indicating direct literary transmission by the compiler.

ai.seo_question: What is the chain of transmission to al-Ṣabāḥ ibn Siyābah in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage gives the sanad/isnad for reports transmitted from al-Ṣabāḥ ibn Siyābah in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh. Its significance lies in documenting the chain of transmission through named transmitters back to al-Ṣabāḥ ibn Siyābah al-Kūfī.
